why: an optional call is `if f is absent then absent else f(x)`: the callee read once as an Option, the arguments and the call's transition only on the present branch. On a data record the present branch is the ordinary method-call reading, so an explicit presence test proves equal; on an opaque receiver, whose field reads go through the outside, the present branch applies the value read once, so it differs from the two lookups of `if (h.m) h.m(x)`
